original_card.question: Can one reproducible environment or artifact-comparison failure be repaired?
methods: Reproduce one portability failure and add a minimal cross-environment fix.
Audit one canonical-payload comparison for omitted proof-relevant fields.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Preserve immutable source hashes and proof-relevant content; a different compressed byte stream alone is not a mathematical mismatch.

first_step.inspect: Read the gzip-container reproducibility examples and distinguish frozen source bytes from regenerated payloads.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Reproduce one specific mismatch or audit one canonical comparison for omitted proof-relevant fields.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Portable exact checks prevent environment failures from blocking valid contributions.
allowed_variations: One interpreter/version mismatch or one payload field comparison.
scope_change_triggers: Removing immutable-source pins because generated compressed bytes differ.

actual_scope: Reject symbolic-link aliases that let declared replay dependencies evade Git changed-path selection.
scope_change_reason: The portable-replay card began with canonical-payload auditing. The concrete discovered failure is at the replay dependency boundary: an accepted directory symlink can hide a required replay. This is a scoped verifier correctness side result, not a mathematical mechanism advance.
bottleneck_link: Correct dependency selection prevents changed proof inputs from bypassing registered checks. Source hashes, scientific payloads and the selected frontier are unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop after the pinned predecessor counterexample, metadata/selection/CLI controls, deleted-input controls and relevant regression suite pass. Do not broaden into general filesystem aliasing or snapshot isolation.
evidence: verify.py reproduces the exact historical skip and checks the repaired boundary; tests/test_research_symlink_inputs.py supplies actual Git/CLI, full metadata, positive and adverse controls. See README.md for observed commands and limits.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used in investigation, implementation, tests and writing; no independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Should declared inputs also require exact Git-index spelling on case-insensitive filesystems?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A filesystem spelling alias may differ from Git changed-path output even when there is no symbolic link. This patch makes no claim about that separate boundary.
open_questions.first_step: Build a real mixed-case Git fixture on a case-insensitive volume and check metadata acceptance plus the target-only changed-path matrix.
open_questions.blocked_by: A separate spelling and platform policy is needed; this package covers symbolic links in stable checkouts.

assignment.note: Deterministic catalogue reproduction. The seed is not novelty evidence.

freshness.overlap_limits: Remote PR scope includes open and closed/merged titles and bodies, with separate coverage and timestamps. State changes are deduplicated by latest PR update; snapshots are not atomic. No code diffs or arbitrary package files are searched. Recheck relevant heads before submission.
